expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".

summary: The candidate quickly diagnosed the sweep bug by reading the failing test's expected vs actual output, correctly named the exact mechanism (original vs remaining count), edited sweep.ts once, and ended the session without ever re-running the tests to confirm the fix worked.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate opened the failing test file and used the concrete expected/actual mismatch (5 vs 8, 3 shipped units) to ground their diagnosis rather than guessing blindly. They did not ask any clarifying question, but the test output itself resolved the ambiguity, so their read was evidence-based rather than assumption-based.

Before touching code, the candidate explicitly named the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count instead of the remaining count — which is precisely the root cause and specific enough to be falsifiable.
The candidate narrated the diff they were seeing and the hypothesis it implied in real time, giving a transcript that clearly explains their reasoning path even though the session was very short.

The edit to sweep.ts was made and saved immediately following the stated hypothesis, with no scattered or contradictory changes, though the session offers no view into the diff's precision beyond the candidate's own description.

After editing and saving, the candidate declared confidence and ended the session without re-running the test suite to confirm the previously-failing test now passed or that other behavior stayed intact.

The candidate's only post-edit comment was a brief assertion of confidence with no articulation of why the remaining-count fix resolves the phantom-stock issue, and the session ended immediately after.
